eyebrow: Northbridge Retail splits one network into several
CIDR: the /n is how many bits are network
code:
/24  -> 8 host bits  -> 256 total -> 254 usable
/25  -> 7 host bits  -> 128 total -> 126 usable
/26  -> 6 host bits  ->  64 total ->  62 usable
/27  -> 5 host bits  ->  32 total ->  30 usable

usable hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2
(minus network address, minus broadcast address)
caption: The slash number states how many of the 32 address bits are the network portion — the rest are host bits.

eyebrow: Sizing the warehouse: ~40 devices, room to 55
code:
Chosen: 192.168.10.0/26  (62 usable hosts)

Network address:   192.168.10.0
Usable hosts:      192.168.10.1 - 192.168.10.62
Broadcast address: 192.168.10.63

Next subnet starts cleanly at: 192.168.10.64/26
caption: A /26 comfortably covers 40 devices plus growth, without the waste of a full /24's 254 addresses.
